Use-case brief · Confluence, space "Vehicle product" · written by the PO · fictitious scenario for the simulation (only the provenance of the data is real)

The Design team must announce the fuel efficiency of a new model as soon as its technical sheet is approved, about six months before the road tests. Today an engineer estimates it by hand by comparing with a similar model; mean gap observed, about 4.5 mpg.
Which prototypes to send first to the fuel-efficiency tests (about twenty tests a year), and which provisional figure to show in the first product sheets.
Estimate the fuel efficiency from the technical sheet alone, clearly better than the manual estimate (aim at a mean gap of about 3.5 mpg), with a range.
A prediction service called by the design tool for each new technical sheet; the estimate and its range are read by an engineer before any use; the model is retrained every year with the new tests.
Current method: about 4.5 mpg of error · Aimed at: about 3.5 mpg
Who uses it, and what an error costs
What it changes for the study
The conclusion will say whether the estimate does better than the current method.
The error measure will have to reflect this cost (step 5).
The prediction moment will be the approval of the technical sheet (step 2).
